title: Grid Illumination Queries
description:
There is a 2D `n x n` grid where every cell is initially turned off. You are given a 2D array `lamps`, where `lamps[i] = [row, col]` turns on a lamp at `(row, col)` (note: `lamps` may contain duplicate coordinates referring to the same lamp). Each active lamp illuminates its own cell plus every cell in the same **row**, same **column**, and both **diagonals**.

You are also given `queries`, where `queries[j] = [qr, qc]`. Process each query sequentially:
1. Record `1` if `(qr, qc)` is currently illuminated by at least one active lamp, or `0` otherwise.
2. Immediately after answering, turn off every active lamp located at `(qr, qc)` or any of its 8 adjacent neighbors (the `3 x 3` neighborhood centered at `(qr, qc)`).

Return an integer array `ans` of length `queries.length` containing the result for each query.
hints: Store active lamp coordinates in a hash set (deduplicating input lamps) and maintain four hash maps counting active lamps on each row r, column c, main diagonal (r - c), and anti-diagonal (r + c).
A query cell (qr, qc) is lit iff any of its four line counters is > 0; then inspect all 9 cells in its 3x3 neighborhood and remove any active lamp while decrementing all four counters.

examples.explanation: Query (1,1) is lit diagonally by both (0,0) and (4,4), returning 1, and turns off the lamp at (0,0); query (1,0) is no longer lit by (4,4), returning 0.
Query (0,4) is lit (1) and turns off lamp (0,4); query (0,1) is still lit by row-0 lamp (0,0) (1) and turns off (0,0); query (1,4) has no remaining active lamps, returning 0.
Duplicate lamp [0,0] is turned on only once, so after query (1,1) turns it off, query (0,0) sees 0 active lamps and returns 0.
